sections.h2: Who sends the Durham property tax bill
sections.html:
One county department handles the whole city. Durham County Tax Administration lists property, assesses it and collects the money, while the City of Durham only decides its own rate. You can visit in person at 201 East Main Street, 3rd Floor, Administration Building II, Durham, NC 27701, any weekday from 8:30 AM to 5:00 PM, or call 919-560-0300.

The county splits the office into six areas: License and Fees, Payment and Collections, Personal Property, Real Property, Tax Help and Tax Relief. Mailed payments go to Durham County Tax Collector, PO Box 3397, Durham, NC 27702-3397. Never mail cash. When a parcel goes to foreclosure, the plaintiffs are the City and County of Durham together, so a bill from either side ends up in the same collection process.

For fiscal year 2026-27 the city rate is $0.4371 and the county rate is $0.5792, a combined $1.0163 per $100 of assessed value. Rates reset each year when the budgets wrap up in mid to late June, and the new figures start July 1.

A parcel inside the City of Durham Business Improvement District pays a combined $1.0863 for 2026-27. A solid waste fee of $185.00 applies for the 2026-27 year, and Morrisville, Cary, Raleigh and Chapel Hill each have their own separate lines.

Bills carry a September 1 due date, but you have until January 5 before interest starts. From January 6, interest runs 2% for the first month and three quarters of one percent for each month after that, as set by G.S. 105-360.

  • A January 5 that falls on a weekend moves the cutoff to the next business day.
  • Monthly payment plans cover real property only and must be set up before the bill goes delinquent.
  • Escrow accounts usually send their payment in late November.
  • Cards add a processing fee, while online electronic checks cost nothing.
  • A returned check costs $25, and from then on the office wants cash or certified funds only.

sections.h2: How to appeal your Durham assessment
sections.html:
Appeals go to the county Board of Equalization and Review. Call Tax Administration for the current filing cutoff, since it changes with each reappraisal cycle and each year's calendar. The county prefers the online appeal on its Tax Help page, which lets you message staff and track your case. A paper form is the fallback.

Durham appraised all real estate as of January 1, 2025. Staff will talk about the appraised value and nothing else, so size of the increase, affordability and service levels are off the table. Outside a reappraisal year, a parcel's value changes only for things like rezoning or new or altered buildings. If you lose before the county board, you have 30 days from the mailing of the decision to notify the state Property Tax Commission, under G.S. 105-290.

The county describes three homestead programs, plus help through the Department of Social Services for low income owners. Applications are due June 1. Call 919-560-0300 with questions.

  • An elderly or disabled exclusion, with a one time application and a $38,800 income cap.
  • A circuit breaker deferment that holds tax to a percentage of income and needs a fresh application every year.
  • A disabled veteran exclusion of up to $45,000 of appraised value.

Deferred circuit breaker tax is repaid when the owner dies, sells or moves, and the most recent three years come due. If you are selling with a deferment, ask the assessor for the balance early.

sections.h2: What happens when Durham property tax goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Taxes you do not pay on real property turn into a lien on the house. After notices and a pre-foreclosure letter, the county can hand the file to a private attorney and foreclose under G.S. 105-374. The owner of record on the delinquency date, January 6, appears in a required newspaper notice, and a payment plan does not prevent that.

  • Bank attachment: your bank holds the account for ten days, or until the tax office says the debt is paid.
  • Wage garnishment: the employer withholds 10% of gross pay each pay period, as the statute provides.
  • State refund setoff: the state takes the refund and tacks on a $5.00 fee plus a $15.00 administrative fee.
  • Sheriff levy: the sheriff can seize and sell personal property, and a towed vehicle adds a $75.00 towing fee.

Once a file is assigned to an attorney, the tax office stops taking direct payments. The payoff must cover taxes, interest, fees and costs, and it is paid through the attorney. Sales happen once a month, on the second Tuesday at 12:00pm, inside the Durham County Judicial Building lobby at 510 Dillard Street. The winning bidder puts down 10%, then a 10 day upset bid window opens. Until the court confirms the sale, the owner can still redeem. Durham County sells no tax liens, because the legislature ended that practice in 1983.

sections.h2: Selling a Durham home with taxes owed
sections.html:
The January 1 owner gets the bill for that whole year. If a bill reaches you after the sale, you are told to hand it to the buyer, so agree on the split before closing instead of trusting the mail. Your closing attorney can divide the year between you and the buyer.

  1. Request a written balance from the tax collector first, then choose your closing date.
  2. If the parcel has already gone to a foreclosure attorney, get the payoff quote from that attorney. Only the attorney can give it, so plan the closing date around that quote.
  3. If you have deferred circuit breaker tax, ask the assessor for the amount that comes due on transfer.
  4. Have the closing attorney pay any balance from your proceeds at the table.

A cash buyer can often close fast enough that a payoff quote stays valid, and a cash sale skips the lender appraisal and underwriting steps. The tax lien still has to be cleared first either way.

The city counts 305,561 residents as of July 2025, a 7.6% gain over 2020. About 52.3% of homes are owner occupied, with a median value of $392,800. Middle household income is $81,619, and gross rent in the middle is $1,508. Those home values are the base the tax rates above apply to.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to pay Durham property tax without interest?
faqs.a: Pay by January 5. Interest starts January 6, even though the bill itself is dated for September 1. Registered vehicles follow a separate schedule.

faqs.q: Who sets the Durham property tax rate?
faqs.a: Both. Council fixes the city portion in its June budget, and the county commissioners fix theirs. You see one combined bill, with new rates starting July 1.

faqs.q: Can I get a payment plan for my Durham property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, for real property only, and you must sign up before delinquency. Before January 5 you may also pay in installments with no agreement at all.

faqs.q: If I sold my Durham house in March, who owes that year's bill?
faqs.a: You do, on paper, because the owner of record on January 1 is billed. The county suggests forwarding it to the buyer, so work out who pays what at closing.

faqs.q: How do I stop a Durham tax foreclosure?
faqs.a: Ask the assigned attorney for a redemption figure and pay it in full before the court confirms the sale. A federal bankruptcy filing can also pause the process.
